stances.claim: The 2013 election calculus actually unites rather than divides Aquino and Binay: both support the same reelectionist senators, an LP-UNA coalition is most logical, and Binay's 2016 ambitions are best served by P-Noy's endorsement.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban rejects the war-mongering narrative of an inevitable Aquino-Binay split, arguing that their continued partnership is invincible and best for both and for the nation. He traces Binay's political history: Cory Aquino named him Makati mayor in 1986; he earned the 'Rambotito' nickname by sporting a submachine gun to defend her during coup attempts; his VP victory was partly due to the NoyBi faction of the Aquino campaign; and he was named to P-Noy's Cabinet as HUDCC chair and OFW presidential adviser. On the 2013 elections: both support the same reelectionist senators; an LP-UNA coalition is most logical; Binay's 2016 ambitions are best served by P-Noy's endorsement since no LP leader has shown presidential designs; and Binay has explicitly denied the canard that he wants Corona retained. CJ calls 'craven insult' the claim that a vote for Corona's acquittal equals a vote for Binay. Their indelible communality -- fighting the Marcos dictatorship, defending human rights, opposing the Arroyo presidency, and sharing the kung walang corrupt walang mahirap agenda -- makes continued unity the rational choice. He counsels Binay that 'early birds do not always catch the worms,' noting Cory, Ramos, and P-Noy himself were latecomers who won.
